title: Antiplatelet Drugs, CYP2C19 and Guided Therapy: What the Evidence Supports
summary: Learn why aspirin and clopidogrel act for the platelet’s lifetime, how CYP2C19 genotype changes clopidogrel choice, why platelet function tests are not interchangeable, and what the GRAVITAS and warfarin genotype trials actually showed.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 39 Hits 9 (clopidogrel/CYP2C19), 10 (aspirin duration), 13 (genotype-guided warfarin), 14 (platelet function assays, GRAVITAS) and Exam Trap 6, checked against CPIC 2022 (clopidogrel) and CPIC 2017 (warfarin), both full text via the NCBI efetch service, CPIC 2011 (abstract only; full text not accessible), Mazzeffi 2017, Jourdi 2022, Gragnano 2022, Bélanger 2020 and Lee 2014. Qualifications: CPIC 2017 reports that EU-PACT improved time in therapeutic range and GIFT reduced a composite outcome, so the reviewer’s “did NOT meaningfully improve time in range in the big trials” is taught as “mixed”; Lee 2014 found aspirin ASPI aggregation normalised by 96 h while Jourdi 2022 Table 1 lists 5–7 days, so no single recovery figure is taught as fixed; the March 2010 boxed-warning date was not found in the sources read and is not taught. Genotype-specific warfarin dose percentages (Number Vault) are not taught.

objectives: Explain why aspirin and clopidogrel inhibit platelets for the platelet’s lifetime.
Translate a CYP2C19 genotype into a metabolizer phenotype and the CPIC recommendation after ACS or PCI.
State why platelet function test results and cut-offs cannot be transferred between devices, and what GRAVITAS and the warfarin genotype trials showed.

scenes.title: Three requests at the platelet bench
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three requests reach the haemostasis bench — (1) a cardiology team asks what a CYP2C19 *2/*3 genotype means for a patient starting clopidogrel after a coronary stent for acute coronary syndrome; (2) a clinic switching from VerifyNow to Multiplate asks whether the old PRU cut-off still applies; (3) a ward asks whether genotype-guided warfarin dosing is proven and routine. Question token: “Which answer is evidence, and which is habit?”

cues.text: Three requests arrive at the platelet bench. A stent patient starting clopidogrel carries CYP2C19 star 2 and star 3.
A clinic switching platelet function analysers wants to keep its old cut-off. And a ward asks whether genotype-guided warfarin dosing is proven.
Which answers rest on evidence, and which rest on habit?

scenes.title: Two drugs that disable platelets for life
scenes.altText: Schematic: a platelet with two blocked pathways. Aspirin card: irreversible inhibition of cyclooxygenase-1, so thromboxane A2 is not made; the effect lasts for the platelet’s lifetime. Clopidogrel card: a thienopyridine prodrug activated in the liver by two oxidative steps; CYP2C19 contributes most; the active metabolite binds the P2Y12 ADP receptor irreversibly. Recovery card: function returns as unexposed platelets replace inhibited ones; transfused normal platelets can restore haemostasis.

cues.text: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits the platelet enzyme cyclooxygenase one, so the platelet can no longer make thromboxane A two.
Clopidogrel is a prodrug. The liver activates it in two oxidative steps, and CYP2C19 contributes most to both. The active metabolite then binds the ADP receptor P2Y12, also irreversibly.
Both drugs have short half-lives, but because the binding is permanent, the effect lasts for the lifetime of each exposed platelet.
Function comes back only as fresh, unexposed platelets replace the inhibited ones, which is also why transfused normal platelets can restore haemostasis.

scenes.title: From CYP2C19 genotype to drug choice
scenes.altText: Genotype card (CPIC 2022): no-function alleles such as CYP2C19*2 and *3; poor metabolizer = two no-function alleles; intermediate metabolizer = one normal-function plus one no-function allele. Recommendation card: for acute coronary syndrome and/or PCI, avoid clopidogrel in intermediate and poor metabolizers and use an alternative such as prasugrel or ticagrelor. Label token: the US FDA boxed warning notes diminished effectiveness in poor metabolizers (US labelling only). Testing token: CPIC leaves the decision to test to the treating clinician.

cues.text: Genotype becomes phenotype. Star 2 and star 3 are no-function alleles. Two no-function alleles make a poor metabolizer; one normal plus one no-function allele makes an intermediate metabolizer.

Less CYP2C19 activity means less active metabolite and less platelet inhibition. The 2022 CPIC guideline says that for acute coronary syndrome or stenting, intermediate and poor metabolizers should avoid clopidogrel and take an alternative such as prasugrel or ticagrelor.
In the United States, the clopidogrel label carries a boxed warning about reduced effectiveness in poor metabolizers. That is American labelling; Philippine rules are not covered here.
CPIC explains how to use a genotype once it is known. Whether to order the test is left to the treating clinician.

scenes.title: Platelet function tests are not one test
scenes.altText: Device cards: VerifyNow P2Y12 (citrated whole blood, ADP plus PGE1, fibrinogen-coated beads, result in PRU); Multiplate (hirudin whole blood, impedance aggregometry with ADP, result in U); VASP phosphorylation (flow cytometry or ELISA, platelet reactivity index); TEG Platelet Mapping (heparinised blood, ADP channel compared with thrombin). Warning card: devices differ in sample, agonist and detection, so results and cut-offs are not interchangeable; consensus cut-offs are device-specific (for example high reactivity above 46 U on Multiplate, above 50% on VASP). Aspirin recovery card: in one study of hypertensive patients stopping 100 mg aspirin before dental extraction, ASPI (arachidonic acid) aggregation had normalised by 96 hours; ACCP guidance cited there suggested stopping 7–10 days before noncardiac surgery in low-risk patients. Hook answers.

cues.text: Platelet function tests differ in sample, agonist and readout. VerifyNow reports P2Y12 reaction units from bead agglutination; Multiplate reports impedance units; the VASP assay reports a reactivity index; TEG platelet mapping compares an ADP channel with thrombin.
So their results are not interchangeable, and each device has its own cut-offs. A PRU threshold means nothing on a Multiplate.

Recovery after aspirin also depends on how it is measured. In one study of hypertensive patients on one hundred milligrams daily before dental extraction, arachidonic acid aggregation had normalised ninety-six hours after the last dose, earlier than the seven to ten days the American College of Chest Physicians guidance cited there suggested before surgery.
Back to the hook. The star 2 star 3 patient is a poor metabolizer, so an alternative drug is recommended, and the clinic must adopt Multiplate cut-offs, not its old PRU value.

props.label: 1 Poor metabolizer → alternative · 2 New device → new cut-offs

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Test platelet function and raise the clopidogrel dose” (✓ GRAVITAS: in 2214 patients with high on-treatment reactivity, high-dose clopidogrel gave the same 2.3% event rate as standard dose; ACC/AHA and ESC do not recommend routine platelet function testing); “Genotype-guided warfarin dosing never helped” (✓ trials are mixed: COAG showed no difference in time in range, EU-PACT improved time in range, GIFT reduced a composite outcome by 27%; CPIC gives genotype-based dosing when results are available); “One PRU cut-off fits every device” (✓ results are not interchangeable).

cues.text: Trap one: test platelet function, then raise the clopidogrel dose. In GRAVITAS, high-dose clopidogrel gave the same event rate, two point three percent, as standard dose, and routine testing is not recommended.
Trap two: genotype-guided warfarin dosing never helped. The trials are mixed. COAG showed no gain in time in range, but EU-PACT improved it and GIFT cut a composite outcome.
Trap three: one cut-off fits every analyser. No: platelet function tests are not interchangeable.

props.title: ✗ “Warfarin genotyping never helped.”
lines: ✓ Mixed: COAG no, EU-PACT and GIFT yes

scenes.title: Permanent marker, missing key
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Aspirin and clopidogrel are PERMANENT MARKERS: a marked platelet stays marked until it is replaced. CYP2C19 is the KEY that unlocks clopidogrel; poor metabolizers are missing the key. Each analyser speaks its own LANGUAGE, so never translate a cut-off.” Tokens: marker = irreversible · key = CYP2C19 · language = device-specific cut-offs. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: aspirin and clopidogrel are permanent markers; a marked platelet stays marked until it is replaced. CYP2C19 is the key that unlocks clopidogrel. And each analyser speaks its own language, so never translate a cut-off.

Where it breaks: function can recover sooner than one platelet lifetime, because new platelets keep arriving; intermediate metabolizers still have half a key yet are steered away from clopidogrel after stenting; and ticagrelor is a reversible blocker, not a marker.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: Recovery can beat one platelet lifetime

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Aspirin and clopidogrel block irreversibly · clopidogrel needs CYP2C19 · poor or intermediate metabolizer after stenting → alternative”, “Platelet function tests not interchangeable · guided dosing trials mixed → not routine”.

cues.text: Aspirin and clopidogrel disable platelets for life and clopidogrel needs CYP2C19 to work, but platelet function tests are not interchangeable and guided-dosing trials were mixed, so neither genotype nor platelet function testing is a routine monitoring test for every patient.

props.label: Irreversible block · CYP2C19 activates clopidogrel · poor metabolizer → alternative
Tests not interchangeable · guided-dosing trials mixed → not routine

explanation.what: Plain language: aspirin and clopidogrel permanently switch off the platelets they touch, so the effect wears off only as new platelets are made. Clopidogrel has to be switched on by a liver enzyme, CYP2C19, and people with non-working copies of that gene get less benefit. Tests that measure platelet function exist, but each machine measures differently; raising the clopidogrel dose on the basis of such a test did not reduce events in a large trial, and genotype-guided warfarin dosing gave mixed results. Scientific terms: cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1), thromboxane A2, thienopyridine prodrug, P2Y12 receptor, CYP2C19 no-function alleles (*2, *3), poor and intermediate metabolizer, high on-treatment platelet reactivity, VerifyNow PRU, Multiplate, VASP phosphorylation, TEG Platelet Mapping, time in therapeutic range (TTR).
explanation.why: Irreversible drug binding outlasts the drug’s plasma half-life, so recovery depends on platelet turnover. Reduced CYP2C19 activity lowers active metabolite formation. Platelet function devices differ in sample, agonist and detection, so their numbers are on different scales.
explanation.measure: CPIC 2022: poor metabolizer = two no-function alleles; intermediate = one normal plus one no-function allele; after ACS and/or PCI, avoid clopidogrel in poor and intermediate metabolizers (prasugrel or ticagrelor). Consensus cut-offs are device-specific (for example high reactivity > 46 U on Multiplate, > 50% on VASP). GRAVITAS: 2214 patients with high on-treatment reactivity; 6-month events 2.3% with high-dose vs 2.3% with standard-dose clopidogrel. One aspirin study: ASPI aggregation normalised 96 h after stopping 100 mg daily (one review table instead lists 5-7 days).
explanation.differs: Aspirin (COX-1, irreversible) vs clopidogrel (P2Y12, irreversible, prodrug) vs ticagrelor (P2Y12, reversible). Genotype (predicts metabolite formation) vs platelet function test (measures current inhibition). COAG (no TTR gain) vs EU-PACT (better TTR) vs GIFT (fewer composite events).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: the phenotype of CYP2C19 *2/*3, why aspirin’s effect outlasts the drug, whether a cut-off can be moved between analysers, and whether platelet-function-guided or genotype-guided dosing is routine.

mnemonic.text: Aspirin and clopidogrel are PERMANENT MARKERS: a marked platelet stays marked until it is replaced. CYP2C19 is the KEY that unlocks clopidogrel; poor metabolizers are missing the key. Each analyser speaks its own LANGUAGE, so never translate a cut-off.
mnemonic.explanation: Links irreversible binding, prodrug activation and device-specific cut-offs.
mnemonic.limitation: Function can recover sooner than one platelet lifetime because new platelets keep entering the blood; intermediate metabolizers have partial activity yet CPIC still advises an alternative after ACS or PCI; ticagrelor blocks P2Y12 reversibly.

analogyLimitations: Platelet and pathway drawings are schematic.

The 96-hour aspirin recovery figure comes from one study with one test (arachidonic acid aggregation) in hypertensive dental-extraction patients; other tests, doses and populations give different figures.
takeaway: Aspirin and clopidogrel disable platelets for life and clopidogrel needs CYP2C19 to work, but platelet function tests are not interchangeable and guided-dosing trials were mixed, so neither genotype nor platelet function testing is a routine monitoring test for every patient.

questions.stem: A patient with acute coronary syndrome receives a coronary stent. CYP2C19 genotyping shows *2/*3. According to the 2022 CPIC guideline, what is recommended?

options.text: Avoid clopidogrel and use an alternative such as prasugrel or ticagrelor
options.rationale: Correct. *2 and *3 are no-function alleles, so this is a poor metabolizer; CPIC advises an alternative after ACS or PCI.

options.text: Give standard-dose clopidogrel; genotype does not affect it
options.rationale: Incorrect. Clopidogrel is a prodrug and CYP2C19 contributes most to its activation.
Incorrect. CPIC recommends an alternative agent, and in GRAVITAS high-dose clopidogrel did not lower events in patients with high on-treatment reactivity.
Incorrect. The patient still needs P2Y12 inhibition after stenting; the question is which drug.

questions.stem: Aspirin has a short plasma half-life, yet its antiplatelet effect persists for days after the last dose. Why?

options.text: It irreversibly inhibits platelet COX-1, so recovery requires new, unexposed platelets
options.rationale: Correct. The block lasts for the exposed platelet’s lifetime; function returns as platelets are replaced.

options.text: It is stored in fat and released slowly
options.rationale: Incorrect. The persistence comes from irreversible binding, not slow release.

options.text: It needs CYP2C19 activation in the liver
options.rationale: Incorrect. That describes clopidogrel, not aspirin.

options.text: It reversibly blocks the P2Y12 receptor
options.rationale: Incorrect. Aspirin targets COX-1; a reversible P2Y12 blocker is ticagrelor.

questions.stem: A laboratory replaces its VerifyNow P2Y12 assay with Multiplate ADP testing. What should it do with its existing PRU-based cut-off for high on-treatment reactivity?

options.text: Retire it and use cut-offs established for the Multiplate assay
options.rationale: Correct. Platelet function tests differ in sample, agonist and readout, so results and cut-offs are not interchangeable.

options.text: Apply the same number to Multiplate units
options.rationale: Incorrect. PRU and Multiplate units are different scales.

options.text: Convert it with a fixed factor of 10
options.rationale: Incorrect. No fixed conversion exists; the devices measure different things.

options.text: Keep it, because all platelet function tests are standardised
options.rationale: Incorrect. The review literature states these tests are not standardised.

claims.text: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits COX-1; clopidogrel is a prodrug activated mainly by CYP2C19 and binds P2Y12 irreversibly; effects last the platelet’s lifetime; transfused platelets can restore haemostasis.
One study: ASPI aggregation normalised 96 h after stopping 100 mg aspirin daily; ACCP suggested 7–10 days before noncardiac surgery; a review table lists 5–7 days for aspirin.
claims.note: Lee 2014 is one study with one test in hypertensive dental-extraction patients; Jourdi 2022 Table 1 lists 5–7 days, so recovery time is taught as method-dependent rather than as one fixed figure.

claims.text: CYP2C19 phenotype definitions; ACS/PCI recommendation for IMs and PMs; testing at clinician discretion; US boxed warning on reduced effectiveness in PMs.
Platelet function devices differ and are not interchangeable; cut-offs are device-specific.
GRAVITAS: 2214 patients, 2.3% vs 2.3%; routine platelet function testing not recommended by ACC/AHA or ESC.
Warfarin genotype trials mixed: COAG no TTR difference, EU-PACT improved TTR, GIFT 27% composite reduction.
Boxed warning date (March 2010); genotype-specific CYP2C9/VKORC1 warfarin dose percentages; warfarin genetic resistance dose.
claims.note: Not taught as facts in this lesson; not found in the sources read.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 39 Hit 13 and Exam Trap 6 say genotype-guided warfarin dosing did not meaningfully improve time in therapeutic range in the big trials (naming Pirmohamed, the EU-PACT trial, among those with no/minimal benefit). CPIC 2017 reports that EU-PACT improved time in therapeutic range and time to stable dose and that GIFT reduced a composite outcome by 27%, while COAG showed no difference; the lesson teaches the results as mixed (register flag rv-warfarin-genotype-trials).

Ch. 39 Hit 10 gives 5–7 days for aspirin’s platelet effect after stopping. Jourdi 2022 Table 1 does list 5–7 days for aspirin, but Lee 2014 found ASPI aggregation normalised 96 h after stopping 100 mg daily in hypertensive dental-extraction patients, and the ACCP guidance cited there suggested stopping 7–10 days before surgery; the figure is test-, dose- and population-dependent rather than fixed (register flag rv-aspirin-recovery-time).

Ch. 39 Hit 9 dates the FDA boxed warning to March 2010; CPIC 2022 confirms the warning and a 2016 FDA label update broadening it to all patients taking clopidogrel, but none of the sources read gives a March 2010 date. The warning is US labelling; Philippine FDA labelling and local guidance are not covered (register flag rv-clopidogrel-boxed-warning).
